title: Figaro Clause Spec (Layer A)
description: The canonical shape of a Figaro clause specification — the off-chain JSON a clause author writes, pins to IPFS, and registers in ClauseRegistry. A clause is one term or condition of an agreement, published once, that anyone can compose. The spec has two halves either side of the UI/protocol crease: the TOP LEVEL is the protocol half (identity, registration, and the content fields that become clauses of signed agreements) — its reference parser is `parseClauseSpec` (sdk/src/clauses/spec.ts); `block` is the UI half (instructions to frontends, organized into phase sections by reader: design / checkout / runtime) — its reference parser is the frontend's `parseBlockBinding` (frontend/lib/shared/clauseBlockBinding.ts). Nothing in `block` is ever read on-chain. A conformance test (sdk/tests/clauses/schema-conformance.test.ts) keeps schema and parsers in lockstep. Validate your clause against this before registering it — a clause that does not conform is not surfaced by conforming frontends (resolved-empty = absence, never an error). THE STANDARD: express every attribute explicitly — zero, empty, or null, never absent (the repo's own clause corpus complies, enforced by test); consumers treat an absent attribute as its empty value, so a sparser spec still surfaces. The schema is OPEN (additionalProperties allowed at every level but one): unknown fields are tolerated and ignored, so the format can grow by versioning without rejecting older clauses. The one closed level is `stages`, whose every key is a stage key. No string and no object key in the spec outside its top-level `block` holds a lone UTF-16 surrogate (a high half with no low half after it, or a low half alone): those are the bytes the clause key hashes, and a spec that holds one does not parse. JSON Schema cannot state this rule over the open attributes, so a validator of this schema accepts such a spec and the parsers refuse it.

clauseId.description: Human-readable clause name, a presentation field inside the document. The on-chain identity is the clause key, keccak256 of the canonical bytes of the spec without its top-level block; the name reaches it only as bytes like every other field, so two specs with one name are two clauses.

version.description: Clause version — an integer lineage counter a reader sees, never semver and never part of the identity: a changed spec is a new key. At most 2^53 − 1, the safe-integer bound every integer the spec declares keeps.

fields.description: The clause's content fields — the terms-and-conditions blanks. Filled in for a transaction, they become one CLAUSE of the signed agreement (a merkle leaf under the on-chain checkoutHash). This is the content the parties sign. An attestation at a stage the spec declares in `stages` is encoded over that stage's fields, stage 0 included, so a stage-0 attestation re-asserts the signed content only when its contentRef is the leaf's data hash. WHO fills each blank is declared by the block phase sections' `fills` lists and `checkout.catalogueMeasures`; any field named in none of them is the buyer's, filled at checkout (the default — always derived as the complement, never stored).

stages.description: Runtime-evidence field shapes, keyed by stage number (uint8, matching AttestationCoordinator's stage). A key has one spelling: the decimal of an integer 0..255, digits only, with no sign, no leading zero and no whitespace ("0", "1", "255"); a spec with any other key does not parse. The content the parties sign is validated over `fields` alone. Content attested at a stage is encoded and validated over that stage's entry where the spec declares one, else over `fields`; a "0" key is no exception. Declare an entry for each stage whose attested content differs from `fields`: the coordination attestations filed during execution against the committed term (a measured-grams reading, a temperature reading, a detected proximity band). Any composed clause declaring a stage surfaces a repeatable witness capability for it, offered to both parties, with zero per-clause code. Express as {} when the clause declares no runtime-evidence stages.

emptyAnchor.description: Declares that the content the parties sign for this clause is the empty anchor {}: the clause commits no content, and every field it declares is the shape of content attested while the process is open (a process-log clause, whose first event is attested at stage 0 like any other). The sign gate accepts {} for such a clause and refuses any other content; a clause that does not declare it is validated over `fields` like any clause, {} included. It is protocol, read by the sign gate in the SDK and in the proof program, never by the clause's article or anything else in `block`. Present only as true, and never beside a top-level field's `default`, since a default fills the signed content and this clause has none.

type.description: The type of the field's value. A `string` value holds no lone UTF-16 surrogate; a value that holds one does not validate. An `integer` value is a JSON number whose value is a whole number within ±(2^53 − 1), however the text writes it (5, 5.0 and 5e0 are one integer); a value outside that range does not validate, and a larger value belongs in a `bigint` field. A `bigint` value is a decimal string within the uint256 range.

label.description: Cosmetic display label (Layer-A only; nothing on-chain reads it).

disposition.description: The public/private disposition of this field's committed value — the clause-spec side of the data seam. "public" (the default when absent): coordination commons, learnable free, published plaintext. "private": paid-edge data, published only behind the fingerprint (encrypted IPFS / content-withheld clause). The chain carries only the clause data HASH either way; disposition governs publication and per-field grain policy (see figaro-geolocation).

blinding.description: Marks the set's BLINDING FIELD. A field set (the top-level `fields`, or one `stages` entry) that declares a private field declares exactly one, at its top level: type "string", format "bytes32-hex", required true, disposition "private", no default. A set with no other private field declares none, and a set never mixes public and private fields. Its value is 32 random bytes the party that fills the set draws fresh for each commitment or attestation (never a designer, catalog or profile value, never zero, never repeated across the clauses of one agreement), so the set's fingerprint (a clause's data hash, a witness's contentRef) cannot be confirmed by hashing guesses of a value with few possibilities. It is content like any other field: it enters the canonical JSON of stage 0 and the ABI bytes of a stage, and travels with the content to whoever is shown it. Present only as true.

default.description: Build/UI default (composition metadata; the ABI encoder ignores it). Shape must match the field type.

format.description: string only. An OPEN axis: any non-empty string is a valid declaration. A validator checks the shape of a value under four formats (bytes32-hex, address-hex, bytes-hex, iso-datetime). It caps the grain of a location code under four more (geohash, h3, s2, olc), by the field's format as `formatFromField` resolves it and by the field's disposition; an array item takes the array field's disposition. The grain is a geohash's length in characters, an H3 cell index's resolution, an S2 cell token's level and an Open Location Code's length. A public value carries at most geohash 6 characters, H3 resolution 8, S2 level 13 or Open Location Code length 6; a private value at most 12, 15, 30 or 15. A value finer than its cap does not validate. Under h3, s2 or olc a value that is no code of the standard does not validate either, since its grain cannot be read; a geohash value's characters are not checked, only its length. A validator treats every other format as a plain string. A location under any other standard is bounded only by the field's own `maxLength`, so a public field that declares one has no grain cap. Frontends may map known formats to richer inputs.

formatFromField.description: string only. VALUE-DRIVEN input format: name a SIBLING field whose committed VALUE is the format key, instead of the static `format`. Lets a field's richer input follow an open, per-composition standard axis (figaro-geolocation's origin/destination declare formatFromField:"geocodeStandard" — the geohash picker + grain cap render when the committed standard is geohash, degrading to plain text otherwise). Resolved as values[formatFromField] ?? sibling default ?? format. The grain cap of `format` applies to the resolved format.

pattern.description: string only. A regex written in the portable core: printable ASCII; literals, '.', classes, groups '(...)' and '(?:...)', \d \D \w \W \s \S, escaped punctuation, ^ $ \b \B, alternation, and the quantifiers * + ? {n} {n,} {n,m} with counts up to 64, each optionally lazy. Its expanded size is at most 4096: each atom, each assertion and each '|' counts one; a group counts one more than what it holds; * + ? count one more than what they follow; and a counted quantifier counts what it follows plus one, times m for {n,m}, n for {n} and n + 1 for {n,}. A value whose length in UTF-16 units times the expanded size is past 4194304 is refused without the pattern run, and a content whose values' sum of that work is past 16777216 is refused. No lookaround, backreference, named group, inline flag, possessive quantifier, Unicode class, nested class or letter escape. A patterned field's value is printable ASCII.

min.description: integer (number) or bigint (decimal string). An integer field's bound is a whole number within ±(2^53 − 1).

max.description: integer (number) or bigint (decimal string). An integer field's bound is a whole number within ±(2^53 − 1).

values.description: enum only — the ordered value codes, at most 256 (a value encodes as its uint8 position).

sentinel.description: enum only — an ABI position-as-index placeholder, never a valid input.

items.description: array only — the element field spec (its name/required are injected, so omit them). A blinding field is never an array element. The element is one level deeper than its array field; a field more than 16 levels below a top-level field does not parse.

fields.description: object only — the nested (named) field specs. A blinding field is never nested. Each nested field is one level deeper than its object field; a field more than 16 levels below a top-level field does not parse. JSON Schema cannot state the depth, so a validator of this schema accepts a deeper spec and the parsers refuse it.

field.description: A named field — top-level, stage-override, or object property. Requires name + type + required.

nestedField.description: A field nested in an object field. A blinding field is a top-level field of its set, so it is never nested.

carriesPrivate.description: A field that declares a private value: its own disposition is "private", or a field nested in it (an object's `fields`, an array's `items`, at any depth) is.

fieldSet.description: One field set: the top-level `fields`, or one `stages` entry. The leaf model withholds a whole set, never one field, so a set does not mix public and private fields; a field counts as private when it or a field nested in it is. A set that declares a private field declares exactly one blinding field; a set with no other private field declares none.

itemField.description: An array ELEMENT spec. The parser injects name + required, so only type is required here.

block.description: The UI half of the spec — instructions to frontends about how the clause presents and composes, organized into PHASE SECTIONS, each named for the phase whose actor it instructs: `design` (the designer composing agreements and assemblies), `checkout` (the seller binding and the buyer filling and signing), `runtime` (the parties while the process runs, after commit). Nothing on-chain reads any of it; any frontend could present the same clause differently. A later phase may read an earlier section; no phase reads a section named for a later one. An attribute read in two phases is declared in the section of its FIRST reader. The one verb `fills` recurs across sections and always means the same thing: the content fields (by name) whose values that phase's actor authors; the buyer owns every content field named in no fills list and no `checkout.catalogueMeasures` entry.

blockDesign.description: Instructs the designer, who composes clauses into agreements and assemblies. Checkout and runtime may read it.

article.description: Drawer grouping heading (free-form, never a closed list) — the contract-document section this clause reads under. The set of articles is whatever the registered clauses declare.

scope.description: What the clause binds. "agreement" (the default) = a term of ONE relationship, composed per-order in the drawer. "assembly" = a term of the COMPOSITION itself (a denomination pin, a dispute forum): composed ONCE at the assembly level of the designer, carried once in the assembly (identity-bearing — part of the processDesignHash), and folded into EVERY agreement at checkout so every party signs it. Composing an assembly-scoped clause on an order — or an agreement-scoped one at assembly level — is a build/publish ERROR, never a silent no-op.

nestsUnder.description: A field name on a parent clause this clause nests under in the drawer — a containment relationship read from the spec, never a hardcoded tree. Null for top-level clauses.

fills.description: The content fields (by name) the DESIGNER authors into the assembly — the tailoring that adapts a generic clause to a specific application (a pinned consent document, a pinned denomination). The drawer exposes field editors exactly for these; their values survive into the published assembly (identity-bearing — part of the processDesignHash). Express as [] when the designer only selects the clause.

composes.description: Composition binding — the on-network contract or external forum this clause composes with (external, on-chain composition). `interface` names a STANDARD composition interface (chain-agnostic, read from spec — never a bundled clause-id switch in code); the concrete instance ADDRESS is chain-specific and comes at runtime, not here. `forumUrl` deep-links a provider's own web UI for URL-only compositions (https: only — it renders as a link). Declared here (the designer composes it); its inputs are collected at checkout (checkout.compositionFields) and it is dispatched at runtime. Null for clauses that compose with nothing.

blockCheckout.description: Instructs the checkout's actors: the seller, who binds an assembly through its catalog and profile, and the buyer, who fills and signs. It says where declared values come from before the buyer signs. Any content field named in none of its lists — and not in design.fills — is the buyer's, filled at checkout (the default case; derived as the complement, never stored). Runtime may read it; design does not.

catalogueFills.description: The content fields (by name) authored per-item on the member's CATALOG (item master data: freight class, hazmat class, cold-chain window) and folded onto the matching leaf at checkout. Generic surfaces render a spec-driven authoring section on the catalog item for ANY clause declaring this — including one this codebase has never seen. Express as [] when no field is catalog-authored.

profileFills.description: The content fields (by name) authored ONCE on the member's PROFILE (the member's master data: a dim-weight divisor, a declared credential id) and folded onto the matching leaf at checkout. The seller-level sibling of catalogueFills (catalog = what is sold, profile = who sells). Express as [] when no field is profile-authored.

from.description: The catalog-item field the measure is read from (a field of the item the seller lists, e.g. massGrams).

combine.description: How the order's lines combine it. "sum": the item's value × the line's quantity, added over every line. "single-unit": the item's value, only when the order is one unit (one line, quantity 1) — a measure that does not add across units, such as a packaged dimension.

catalogueMeasures.description: The content fields (by name, the map's keys) read from each order line's CATALOG ITEM and combined at checkout: the item's own attributes (its mass, volume, dimensions), as opposed to catalogueFills' per-clause values. A measure the order's lines cannot supply — a line whose item lacks the field, or a single-unit measure on an order of several units — stays missing: nothing is invented, and a REQUIRED one refuses the order before it is signed. Absent is read as {}.

reader.description: The STANDARD whose reader a frontend applies (an open registry keyed by this name, never a clause id), e.g. "kleros-liquid-policy-courts": a KlerosLiquid arbitrator's court list and each court's policy name in its PolicyRegistry.

contracts.description: For each chain, by its decimal chain id, the contracts the reader reads, each by the reader's own role name (e.g. arbitrator, policyRegistry).

values.description: For each enum value, what the reader looks for on the chain, in the reader's own terms (for kleros-liquid-policy-courts, the court's policy names from the root down; the root court is named alone).

heldValues.description: The enum content fields (by name, the map's keys) whose values a checkout offers only when the chain in use holds what each value names, read at checkout by the named reader from the contracts given for that chain. A presentation hint, read only by a frontend that knows the reader's standard: it changes nothing the parties sign, and another frontend may ignore it. On a chain the hint gives no contracts for, every value is offered; under a reader the frontend does not know, a failed read or an empty one, no value is. The addresses are part of the spec's registered bytes, so a chain added later needs a new spec version. Absent is read as {}.

field.description: The top-level array content field that holds the order's lines.

quantity.description: The field of each line item that carries its quantity (an integer field).

unitPrice.description: The field of each line item that carries its unit price (a bigint field, in the token's smallest unit).

item.description: The field of each line item that carries the catalog item's id (a string field).

name.description: The field of each line item that carries the catalog item's name (a string field).

pricedLines.description: The mark on the order's PRICED LINES: the array field that holds them and which field of each line item plays each role. Code reads the mark, never a field name. The checkout writes the lines into the marked field, a quote request prices each line's unit price, and a review reads them through the mark. A mark the spec's own fields contradict marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no priced lines.

rule.description: The rule's name in the open derivation registry (registerCheckoutDerivation), never a clause id.

inputs.description: The rule's inputs, by the rule's own input names: each one a content field of the same clause ({ field }, read after the catalog and profile folds) or a catalog measure ({ from, combine }, combined as catalogueMeasures combines).

derives.description: The content fields (by name, the map's keys) the checkout COMPUTES, each by a rule of the open derivation registry over its declared inputs. Never the buyer's. A rule the registry does not hold, or inputs it cannot derive from, leave the field as it was. Absent is read as {}.

start.description: The content field that holds the window's start (a string field of format iso-datetime).

end.description: The content field that holds the window's end (a string field of format iso-datetime).

timeWindow.description: The mark on the clause's TIME WINDOW: which content field is its start and which is its end. A quantity source that bills by the window (booking-window) reads the mark, never the format or the order of the fields. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, named twice, or not of format iso-datetime) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no window, and a source that needs one prices nothing.

from.description: The content field that holds the route's origin (a string field whose formatFromField names the field that declares its standard).

to.description: The content field that holds the route's destination (a string field whose formatFromField names the field that declares its standard).

endpoints.description: The mark on the clause's ROUTE: which content field is its origin and which is its destination. A quantity source that bills by distance (order-geodistance) reads the mark, never the format or the order of the fields. A later phase may read it too: a trade document shows the route's two ends through it. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, named twice, or not a string field) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no route, and a source that needs one prices nothing.

uri.description: The content field that holds the outside register's URI template (a string field of format uri-template, with an {id} placeholder).

id.description: The content field that holds the identifier the register is looked up by (a string field).

registerLink.description: The mark on a LINK TO AN OUTSIDE REGISTER: which content field holds the register's URI template and which holds the identifier. A reader offers a link to the register's own entry from the mark, never from the names of the fields. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, named twice, not a string field, or a URI field not of format uri-template) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause offers no such link.

dataSources.description: The content field that names the PROCESSES WHOSE DATA the clause grants access to (an array field whose items are string fields of format bytes32-hex, each a processId). The buyer reads each named process's resolution before it signs, and a reader proves each disclosed leaf against the named processes' checkoutHash, through the mark, never through the name of the field. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, or not such an array) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause names no data sources.

compositionFields.description: The composition's input field specs: values the buyer supplies at checkout for the contract design.composes names (its opening parameters). They are NOT content fields, so nothing commits them into the agreement. ONE generic form renders them; the form reads no interface name. Same field shape as content fields: one parser, one renderer. Reporting while the process runs is the witness stages (`stages`), never these. Express as [] when the clause takes no composition input.

blockRuntime.description: Instructs the parties while the process runs, after commit: the interactions their tasks use. No earlier phase reads it.

interaction.description: The party↔party runtime interaction standard this clause's tasks use (e.g. a QR order-identity challenge at a hand-off, a per-order ECDH channel). `interface` names a STANDARD interaction, read from the spec — never a bundled clause-id switch. A frontend that registered a surface for the interface mounts it; one that didn't renders nothing extra — progressive enhancement, the protocol never depends on it. Null for clauses whose tasks need no dedicated interaction.

modality.description: The content field that holds the order's MODALITY: how the order is fulfilled (on site, picked up, delivered, virtual, or any value the clause declares). A reader shows the committed value through the mark, never through the name of the field. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, or not a string or enum field) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no modality.

law.description: The content field that names the law that governs the agreement (a string or enum field).

forum.description: The content field that names the forum that hears a dispute (a string or enum field). Optional.

language.description: The content field that names the language of the proceedings (a string or enum field). Optional.

jurisdiction.description: The mark on the clause's JURISDICTION: which content field names the governing law, and, when the clause carries them, which names the forum and the language. A reader summarizes the jurisdiction through the mark, never through the names of the fields. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, named twice, or not a string or enum field) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no jurisdiction.

documentPart.description: The section of a trade document this clause fills, in the words a document layout uses (for example cargo, freight-class, delivery-terms or carriage). A layout shows the clause's committed fields under that section, and may emit a document only where a clause declares a section. It names no field. Absent or null: the clause fills no section.

ladder.description: The content field whose ordered values are the clause's runtime LADDER (an enum field): the value at index k is the event a party attests at stage k, and each party advances its own ladder from its own attestations. A reader offers and labels the next event through the mark, never through the shape or the name of the field. A mark the spec's own fields contradict (a field not declared, or not an enum field) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no ladder.

stage.description: The stage at which a party attests the digest of the content it delivered.

field.description: The field of that stage's set that holds the keccak256 of the delivered bytes (a string field).

contentDigest.description: The mark on the clause's DELIVERY EVIDENCE: the stage and the field where a party attests the keccak256 of the content it delivered over a private channel. The receiver rehashes what it received and checks the attestation through the mark, never through the name of the field. A mark the spec contradicts (a field that the stage's set, its `stages` entry or else the content fields, does not declare as a string field) marks nothing. Absent or null: the clause carries no delivery evidence.
